# HLT-C2 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the supplied PDF, saved in _text/HLT-C2.txt. Page numbers refer to the journal pagination (Page x of 12).

## Rows proposed
- findings: 25 (N 13, Q 12). transformations: 0. claims: 18. relations: 10. decisions: header only.

## Look at first
1. Splitting of the abstract outcome sentence (p.1). "Improvements in participants' well-being, and perceived levels of health and social connectedness as well as reductions in anxiety was demonstrated" was split into C1-C4 because the four outcomes rest on different measures. A single claim would rest on F1, F4, F7, F8, F11, F13 and be joint. The split changes the joint-claim count (C1 and C3 joint, C2 and C4 N only).
2. C7 (men may benefit more). The results section uses only the qualitative "Engaging men" theme (F21, p.9) for this. The quantitative results do not support it: no sex difference in wellbeing change (F2, p = 0.96) and a higher but non-significant male gain in health rating (F9, p = 0.18). The text does not cite F2 or F9 for the claim, so rests_on is F21 only and fit single-strand. If A1 judges that F9 is used implicitly, the claim becomes joint with fit discord (F2) or expand. The Discussion adds "Such claims, however, would require further validation" (p.10).
3. C11 and C13 (summary "positive outcomes" claims). rests_on lists the outcome findings of C1-C5 because the conclusions summarise those results; the text does not cite findings directly at these sentences. Alternative: leave rests_on empty and rely on the covers relations R1-R5. This choice decides whether C11 and C13 count as joint. C13 has no covers relations proposed, to avoid duplication; A1 may extend R1-R5 to C13.
4. C6 (GP use inconclusive). Rests on F15 (N) and F18 (Q); the text links the two directly ("Similar to the quantitative results", p.7). fit confirm.
5. C8 uses "sustained" relationship. The results show flexibility and the coordinator role (F19, F20, F22); continuity appears only in the Discussion ("consistency of the service as well as follow ups", p.10), which is outside scope. F23 (wish for more sessions) was not added.
6. R10 (C16 clashes C15). Basis is the "However" contrast in the Conclusion (p.11). It may be read as a qualification rather than a clash; borderline.
7. R8 (C11 backs C10) uses a Discussion sentence (p.10) as basis, since the abstract only places the two sentences side by side.
8. C12 and C18 are close in content (re-orientation of primary care); no relation proposed because the text does not link them.

## Transformations
None proposed. The study reports no conversion across strands: themes are not counted, and no scores are built from qualitative data. Within-strand operations (age dichotomised into under 50 / 50 and over, p.4; scale scores from validated instruments) are not recorded as transformations because their inputs are not registered findings. The Results section states that the two strands "have been synthesised" (p.4), but no procedure is described.

## Other
- Eligibility: the funder of the service itself is not stated (see proposal).
- Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text with line-break hyphenation removed; "[...]" marks omissions in claims.
- Low follow-up completion (342 of about 2250-3750 users in contact, p.4) is a limitation stated by S1 (p.11), not registered as a finding.
